serenity-absolics-glass-substrate-slip-t:
The glass substrate schedule has slipped another six months, and this time the company that moved is not Samsung Electro-Mechanics but Absolics, the SKC subsidiary.
A start of mass production once set for the second half of 2026 is now put at the first half of 2027,
with a goal of finishing final validation by the end of this year attached to it.
Neither date has been confirmed by the company itself.

@@REF@@Glass substrates eye 2027 launch, scale toward 2030 as CoWoS costs rise and hyperscaler demand grows (TrendForce, 2026-06-05)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/06/05/news-glass-substrates-eye-2027-launch-scale-toward-2030-as-cowos-costs-rise-and-hyperscaler-demand-grows/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/05111635/Intel-glass-substrate-1-624x416.jpg

## What making a substrate out of glass means

A semiconductor die does not attach to a motherboard bare.
A thin plate goes in between to carry signals and power across, and today that plate is mostly built from plastic based material.

Switch that plate to glass and it gets thinner while using power more efficiently.
It also warps less under heat, which suits AI accelerators that spread several dies across a wide area.
The TrendForce piece above puts the gain at 25 percent less thickness and more than 30 percent better power efficiency.
The reason it gives for moving is cost. CoWoS, the method used today to tie dies together across a wide area, now runs at a per-unit price on a par with a 7nm class wafer.

## The step that is stuck is not the making

@@FLOW@@Glass blank|A flat panel much like display glass arrives|Drilling|Fine holes linking top to bottom are cut with a laser|Wiring and mounting|Metal fills the holes and circuitry is drawn on|Customer reliability testing|The customer applies heat and stress to see whether it cracks@@Of the four steps, the one that binds is the last. The maker can be ready and the date still moves, because the buyer has to sign off.

When Samsung Electro-Mechanics revised its start to 2028 at the late July second quarter briefing, the reason it gave was customer reliability testing of its prototypes.
Two companies are stuck at the same step.

Glass is hard, and hard things break.

Run heat up and down a panel drilled through with fine holes and cracks can start around those holes.
That is exactly what the customer is testing for.
A verdict arrives only after hundreds of cycles of mounting a die and taking the temperature up and back down.
The plant sits built and waiting through all of it.
That is why the schedule does not move at the maker's pace.

## The new date is the first half of 2027

@@TIME@@2026-06-05|TrendForce puts Absolics at year-end production and Samsung Electro-Mechanics at 2H 2027|Late July 2026|Samsung Electro-Mechanics revises its start to 2028 at its Q2 briefing|2026-08-14|Serenity reads Absolics as having slipped to 1H 2027|>December 2026|Absolics targets completion of final validation@@In two months both companies moved back by half a year each. The industry's starting line has resettled on 2027.@@TrendForce 2026-06-05, Serenity post 2026-08-14, accessed 2026-08-15

There is no need to read the slippage as bad news only.
Serenity wrote that the shift to glass core substrates itself feels imminent.
Revenue for the equipment and component suppliers is booked at the tool orders that come before the start date rather than at the start date itself, so the moment a date firms up is a starting gun for them.

Two things follow.
If Absolics clears final validation at year end and begins production within the first half of 2027, this delay turns out to have been the last checking step, and orders at the suppliers standing in front of it move first.
If the year end validation pushes the date out again, the question stops being scheduling and becomes the reliability of glass as a material, and the industry's shared 2027 starting line moves with it.

Taiwan's DigiTimes carried the report on August 14,
and in the same piece the bigger movement was not in the process name but in the packaging that wraps the chip.

## One rack, one petabyte a second

Nvidia treats an entire server rack as a single computer.
NVLink is the dedicated path the chips inside it use to hand data to one another.
If that path is narrow, adding more chips buys nothing, because they spend their time waiting on each other.

@@BAR@@Blackwell NVL72|130TB/s|130|Vera Rubin|260TB/s|260|Rubin Ultra|520TB/s|520|Feynman|over 1,040TB/s|1040@@Each generation is exactly double the last. There is a point where copper wiring can no longer carry that width, and switching to light at that point is what CPO is.@@Figures as reported by CloudNews, 2026-08-15, accessed 2026-08-15

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_%283706444821%29.jpg/960px-Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_%283706444821%29.jpg|Accelerators bundled at rack scale. What grows in Feynman is not only the performance of a single chip but the width of the paths running inside this bundle.|ChrisDag · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_(3706444821).jpg

## Packaging binds before the process does

A16 is TSMC's improved node sitting above 2nm.
It offers 8 to 10 percent more speed at the same voltage, or the same speed at 15 to 20 percent less power.

That part is familiar. Getting Feynman out of the door needs what comes after it.
SoIC stacks dies vertically instead of laying them side by side, and the shorter distance between them widens the path.
The catch is that capacity for this step runs on its own schedule, separate from capacity for the chips themselves.

@@TIME@@2026-08-14|DigiTimes reports Feynman on A16 with a larger share of 3D stacking|>2H 2027|Part of AP7 P2, set aside for SoIC, may be turned over to CPO and CoWoS lines|>End of 2027|TSMC targets monthly SoIC capacity of 50,000 wafers|>2H 2028|Feynman expected to launch@@The first three lines decide the last one. If the packaging lines are not standing first, a ready process still ships nothing.@@As reported by DigiTimes 2026-08-14 and CloudNews 2026-08-15

@@REF@@NVIDIA Feynman targets 2028 with A16, 3D chiplets, custom HBM and CPO optical (CloudNews, 2026-08-15)|https://cloudnews.tech/nvidia-feynman-targets-2028-with-a16-3d-chiplets-custom-hbm-and-cpo-optical/|https://cloudnews.tech/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/jensen-nvidia-chips.jpg

That piece puts Feynman's arrival in the second half of 2028 and lays out the same doubling of interconnect width shown above.
Put the two together and it explains why TSMC is hurrying construction at AP7 in Chiayi and AP8 in the Southern Taiwan Science Park.
The bottleneck sits in where things get joined, not in how they are designed.

## Where AP7 P2 ends up

This is the line Jukan flags as interesting.
Some of the AP7 P2 space planned for SoIC may be handed to CPO and CoWoS instead.
If that firms up, sending signals as light enters the real production calendar earlier than the industry had assumed.

Two branches are left.
Hold the 50,000 wafer a month SoIC target through the end of 2027 and Feynman's 2028 schedule largely holds with it, pulling forward when the optical component suppliers get to book revenue.
Let that target slip and the finished part slides even with A16 ready, confirming that this generation's bottleneck was back-end assembly rather than the process node.

The number to watch on this card is TSMC's back-end capacity, not Nvidia's announcements.
schiff-fed-makeup-strategy-retired-befor:
The rule that has the Fed target an average of 2% in order to make up for past low inflation does not exist right now.
The Fed deleted that sentence from its statement on August 22, 2025.

On August 14 Peter Schiff took the rule to be alive and worked out a sum from it.
Inflation has averaged 4% over the past 65 months, so bringing the average back to 2% would take 65 months at 0%.

@@TIME@@2020-08-27|The Fed introduced average inflation targeting at Jackson Hole|2025-08-22|Powell said the Fed had returned to flexible inflation targeting and eliminated the makeup strategy|2026-01-27|The FOMC reaffirmed a statement identical to the August 2025 version|2026-08-14|Schiff published the 65-month sum, resting it on the average 2% target@@The rule the sum rests on left the statement about a year before the sum was written.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Federal Reserve, Powell speech (2025-08-22) · Federal Reserve, FOMC press release (2026-01-27)

## What making up was supposed to mean

Average inflation targeting, adopted in August 2020, was a promise to read the target over a stretch of time rather than at a moment.
If inflation ran below the target for a while, it would be allowed to run above it for a while afterwards so that the average came out right.

@@REF@@What do changes in the Fed's longer-run goals and monetary strategy statement mean? (Brookings, 2020-09-02)|https://www.brookings.edu/articles/what-do-changes-in-the-feds-longer-run-goals-and-monetary-strategy-statement-mean/|https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/shutterstock_117869614.jpg?quality=50&w=500

Brookings, writing when the framework was new, described a promise with no period attached to it.
Inflation undershooting "for a time" would be answered by overshooting "for some time", and how many months went into the average was left open.
Powell himself called it a flexible form of average inflation targeting.
Because the averaging window was never pinned down, the stretch to be repaid does not fall out of the rule on its own.

## What the Fed said on the day the sentence went

On August 22, 2025, presenting the results of the framework review, Powell said the Fed had returned to flexible inflation targeting and eliminated the makeup strategy.
In the same remarks he said there had been nothing intentional or moderate about the inflation that arrived.

@@REF@@Speech by Chair Powell on the economic outlook and framework review (Federal Reserve Board, 2025-08-22)|https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/powell20250822a.htm|https://www.federalreserve.gov/images/social-media/social-default-image-opengraph.jpg

What went was not a phrase but the ground the sum stands on.
With a makeup clause, past inflation stays on the books as a debt to be repaid.
Without one, 2% from here is enough.
Then on January 27, 2026, at its annual organisational meeting, the FOMC reaffirmed a statement identical to the August 2025 version.
It has stayed deleted for close to a year.

## The arithmetic that survives January 27, 2026

The quarrel is not with the stretch Schiff measured or the average he found.
It is with where those values get entered.

Under the rule as it stands, five years of past inflation is a record rather than a balance owed.
So the sum reads better as a note on what the Fed has decided not to do than as a forecast of what it will do.
Had the makeup clause survived, today's price level would be a reason to hold rates high for years; with it deleted, that reason no longer comes out of the statement.
Whether the Fed turns back toward repaying the past is decided at the next framework review.
elerian-umich-aug-prelim-51-jobs-fear-lo:
The University of Michigan's preliminary August reading of consumer sentiment came in at 51.0.
That is down from 55.2 in July and below the 55.0 the market expected.
Two straight months of improvement ended here.

@@REF@@U.S. consumer sentiment falls in August 2026, ending recovery (Quartz, 2026-08-14)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-consumer-sentiment-falls-august-171815784.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/F13E1F883A890878DE51BB2494C7B712ACF77EF1879929AF59770727920BB66E/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h675;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fquartz_855%2F79d0c0fb0a8ae3795d2a4c4a2be1bff7.jpg

The survey asked, in the first days of August, how households were taking the spread of the Middle East conflict into prices.

@@CHK@@Consumer sentiment (Aug prelim)|51.0|July|55.2|Consensus|55.0|Current conditions (Aug)|51.8|Expectations (Aug)|50.6|Expectations (July)|55.4@@The half of the survey that asks how things look ahead fell further than the half that asks how things are now. What drove this month's drop was the forward view rather than the present one.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, August 2026 preliminary released 2026-08-14 · consensus is the market forecast

## Why prices rather than jobs

The sentiment index comes in two parts.
One asks how a household is doing now, the other asks how it expects to be doing.

The expectations half fell by more.
Had the drop come from fear of losing work, the half that asks about present circumstances should have moved first and moved harder.
The original post noted that concern about employment stayed relatively low.

The survey holds one more number that shows what kind of decline this is.
Asked whether their own income will rise faster than prices over the coming year, 8% said yes.
In December 2024, 18% said yes to the same question.
Fewer than one household in ten now expects to end the year better off.

## What four weeks did to the price of gasoline

Asked how much prices will rise over the next year, respondents answered 4.3%, a little above July's 4.2%.
The five-to-ten-year answer stayed at 3.3%, unchanged from July.
The distant future held still while the coming year moved.

Inflation expectations track the prices people see most often.
In the United States, the price seen most often is the number on the sign outside a filling station.
The national average price of gasoline rose from $3.855 a gallon on July 13 to $4.006 on August 10.

@@REF@@US consumers sour on economy as inflation concerns remain in focus, UMich survey says (Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-14)|https://www.aol.com/articles/us-consumers-sour-economy-inflation-144047000.html|https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/08/14/d06481c0-11d0-3dab-81b2-59fa44bc65e5/5c2cc9ab-c0ac-400a-b126-926048bd35e3.jpg

Survey director Joanne Hsu said the weakening reached across demographic groups but that the largest reductions came among older consumers, lower-income consumers and those without a college degree.
When the price of something a household cannot stop buying goes up, the households where that item takes the biggest share of the budget shake first.
The cost-of-living explanation in the original post points the right way, but it leaves one step out. What lifted that cost of living is fuel that came through the Middle East conflict.

## What to watch in Michigan's final August reading

A low sentiment index and falling consumption are not the same statement.
The index carries how people feel about prices as well, so a decline pushed by prices and a decline pushed by job losses arrive as the same number.

If the final August reading due at the end of the month settles below the 51.0 preliminary, this drop is confirmed; if it climbs back above 51.0, the preliminary overshot.
The number to read alongside it is the 4.3% year-ahead inflation expectation. If that rises further with gasoline, prices are holding sentiment down; if it falls back below that level, the shock of early August was a one-month affair.

The United States is putting tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and their parts.
President Trump signed the proclamation on August 13 under Section 232 of the trade law, and it takes effect on September 3.

@@REF@@Trump imposes 100% tariffs on some drones and components (Manufacturing Dive, 2026-08-14)|https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/trump-tariffs-drones-uas-components-defense-supply-chain-war/827889/|https://imgproxy.divecdn.com/XaUMScHq_wcCE7VkBxeR9VLh7YMgvcBs6LIGN1z4ylM/g:ce/rs:fit:770:435/Z3M6Ly9kaXZlc2l0ZS1zdG9yYWdlL2RpdmVpbWFnZS9HZXR0eUltYWdlcy0yMjY4MTgwMzA2LmpwZw==.webp

There is not one rate. The proclamation splits into four brackets by product type and by origin.

@@BAR@@General origin, drones over 25kg and thermal-imaging drones|100%|100|General origin, smaller drones and a broad set of components|25%|25|EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein|15%|15|United Kingdom|10%|10@@For the same object, the rate spreads tenfold depending on where it came from. What this proclamation targets is not drones but the origin of drones.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · White House fact sheet (2026-08-13) · Manufacturing Dive (2026-08-14)

## The test for the top bracket is weight and heat

Two things put a drone in the top bracket.
One is a maximum take-off weight above 25kg, roughly 55 pounds.
The other is thermal imaging.

A hobby camera drone usually weighs around a kilogram, so it does not meet either test.
What does is the airframe carrying pesticide over a field, the one hauling materials, and the one that can see the heat of people and equipment at night.
Weight and heat, taken together, are a net for catching airframes that could be used for military or surveillance work.
Docking stations, which drones need in order to take off and land unattended, and critical components fall into the same bracket.

## What it takes to sit in the allied bracket

There is a separate bracket with lower rates.
The European Union, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland and Liechtenstein get 15%, and the United Kingdom gets 10%.

@@REF@@Fact sheet: imposing tariffs on drones and their parts and components (The White House, 2026-08-13)|https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-bolsters-national-security-and-strengthens-u-s-supply-chains-by-imposing-tariffs-on-drones-and-their-parts-and-components/|https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/WH47-Social-Share-Card.jpg

The rate comes with a condition. The White House fact sheet says substantially all of the hardware, the software and the technology has to originate in that country or in the United States.
A drone does not fly on its airframe alone. Flight control software, maps and communication modules come with it.
So an aircraft assembled in Korea or Japan still misses the lower bracket if the software inside it fails the origin test.

## American makers pass through the same gate

The original post read the move as good news for US drone component suppliers and aircraft makers.
The direction is right, but one bracket is missing from that reading.
The 25% rate covers a broad set of components, and American manufacturers import a great many of them.
The proclamation gives 180 days to non-sensitive components and to products carrying Department of War or FCC exemptions.
That builds a six-month gap between the moment costs rise and the moment domestic production is meant to stand up.
The same proclamation directs the commerce secretary to set up an onshoring incentive programme, which reads as a device for filling that gap.

## What splits after September 3

What splits here is whether this tariff raises American drone revenue or American drone costs.
If US airframes fill the space that the top tariff clears of imported finished drones, revenue moves first.
If procurement costs rise by the tariff before that, margin moves first.
If gross margins at US drone makers rise from the prior quarter in the first results after September 3, it is the former; if they fall, it is the latter.
jukan-samsung-nrdk-line2-send-fab-2nm-ba:
Korean media report that Samsung is considering turning one of its research lines into a 2nm production line.
It is Line 2 at NRD-K, the research and development complex in Giheung.
What that line would print is the chip that sits at the very bottom of an HBM stack.

@@REF@@Samsung may repurpose an R&D line for foundry, targeting 2nm HBM base dies for future NVIDIA demand (TrendForce, 2026-08-14)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/14/news-samsung-may-repurpose-rd-line-for-foundry-targeting-2nm-hbm-base-dies-for-future-nvidia-demand/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/02160941/Samsung-HBM4-624x468.png

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg/960px-DDR5_SDRAM_%28with_scale%29_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg|A DRAM stick of the kind that slots into a server. HBM takes chips like these, stands eight to twelve of them on top of each other, and binds them together over one separately made chip at the base.|Smial · FAL 1.3|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DDR5_SDRAM_(with_scale)_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg

## The chip at the bottom of HBM

HBM is memory built by stacking eight to twelve DRAM dies vertically.
At the very bottom sits one more die that is not DRAM.
It marshals the signals the stacked DRAM sends and receives and pushes them out of the package. It is called the base die.

A base die is logic, not memory.
So it is made on a foundry process rather than in a DRAM plant.
Until now a 4nm-class process was enough, but as stacks got taller and speeds higher, heat became the problem.
Doing the same work on less power calls for a finer process, and the answer being floated is 2nm.

## Where the wafers travel

The arrangement described in the report is a "send fab".
Rather than building a product end to end, such a line takes in wafers from other production lines, runs one specific stretch of the process, and sends them back.

@@FLOW@@Production line|Wafers come off Samsung's foundry production lines|NRD-K Line 2|The handed-over wafers get their base die patterned on a 2nm process|HBM stacking|Eight to twelve DRAM dies are stacked on top and bound into one package|Customer|It ships to AI accelerator makers such as NVIDIA@@Once the base die moves to 2nm, what sets HBM's speed is the foundry process, not the DRAM process.

This is where the news actually bites.
The memory contest is shifting from a race to shrink DRAM into a race for a slot on the newest foundry node.
2nm is the node where smartphone application processors and AI chips are already queueing. Memory now wants to join that queue.

@@TIME@@2026-06-02|Samsung showed HBM5 for the first time at Computex|2026-08-14|Korean media reported the review of turning NRD-K Line 2 into a foundry send fab|>2028|Expected start of HBM5 mass production|>H2 2028|Target for bringing the NRD-K complex online@@If the review is real, Samsung is claiming the slot roughly two years before HBM5 starts selling.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · TrendForce (2026-08-14) · TrendForce (2026-06-02)

@@REF@@Samsung unveils HBM5 for the first time at Computex, production reportedly seen around 2028 (TrendForce, 2026-06-02)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/06/02/news-samsung-unveils-hbm5-model-for-the-first-time-at-computex-production-reportedly-seen-around-2028/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/02141324/Samsung-HBM5-model-624x617.png

Earlier reporting says HBM5 is expected to run more than 50% faster than HBM4E.
Samsung has said it will spend 20 trillion won building three NRD-K lines by 2030.
One of those three would be changing jobs.

## What one NRD-K line costs

A research line is where the next generation gets tested.
Turn it over to production and the orders in front of you get filled, but the test bench for the generation after that loses a slot.
This is still at the review stage, and the company has announced nothing.

What splits here is whether Samsung fights the HBM war as a memory company or as a company that owns a foundry.
If it absorbs the 2nm base die in-house, it finishes inside its own walls the step SK Hynix hands to TSMC.
If Line 2 instead starts up as planned for research and development, this report stays a report.
jukan-google-amd-tpu-v10-chatter-vs-broa:
Broadcom has cut its own outlook for the volume of TPUs it will hand to Google.
It said output would come in below prior expectations in both the second half of 2026 and in 2027, and pointed not to demand but to allocating more of its capacity to other customers.

@@CHK@@Projected Google TPU shipments (2026)|4.3 million|Projected Google TPU shipments (2028)|over 35 million|Broadcom's earlier expectation for 2027|6 million@@The overall projection is going up while the number Broadcom quotes for itself has come down. What shrank is not TPU demand but the share of it Broadcom hands to Google.@@The Next Web reporting of 2026-04-20 and Broadcom earnings call remarks as quoted by Jukan, accessed 2026-08-15

A TPU is the AI-specific chip Google designs for its own data centres.
Google does the architecture, but turning it into an actual chip has been outside work, and Broadcom has held that seat for years.

## Demand is not what shrank

The line worth reading twice in Broadcom's explanation is "greater allocation towards other customers".
Google and other buyers are queueing for the same capacity, and Broadcom has been giving more of it to the back of the queue.

Seen from the side placing the order, that is not good news.
The chip sells; the slot to build it does not exist. So Google gets safer by keeping more than one house that can draw its silicon.

@@REF@@Google is building a four-partner chip supply chain to challenge Nvidia in AI inference (The Next Web, 2026-04-20)|https://thenextweb.com/news/google-inference-chips-nvidia-challenge-supply-chain|https://media.thenextweb.com/2026/04/google-inference-chips-nvidia-challenge-supply-chain.jpg

That piece had already mapped the structure this was heading toward.
Google has been splitting training and inference chip design across different firms while pooling fabrication at TSMC no matter who drew the part.
The cost-optimised inference design went to MediaTek, which the article says delivers the same job 20 to 30 percent cheaper.
Marvell, the firm Jukan names, sits inside this picture too.
It designs data centre silicon, and the article reports it has been in talks with Google over an inference chip and a memory processing unit.

## Why Google keeps adding designers

That is where this week's item attaches.
Citing the research house SemiAnalysis, market chatter is said to have Google working with AMD on the TPU v10 generation.
None of it is confirmed, and neither Google nor AMD has said anything about it.

The substance of the chatter runs like this.
AMD has its own custom silicon team but has never properly joined somebody else's custom AI chip project, and this would be the first.
What AMD is said to bring is advanced packaging, the business of stacking and bonding dies into one part, plus CPU design to sit inside the package.
Reinforcement learning work runs better with CPU cores next to the accelerators, and Google and its customers are reported to be asking for exactly that shape.

@@REF@@MediaTek advances 400G SerDes on 2nm, targeting Google TPU v10 and Meta AI ASIC orders (TrendForce, 2026-08-03)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/03/news-mediatek-advances-400g-serdes-on-2nm-targeting-google-tpu-v10-and-meta-ai-asic-orders/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/20135115/MediaTek_MasterBrand_EN_BlackBG_Combo_0923-624x624.png

Another firm is reaching for the same seat.
MediaTek is preparing circuitry on 2nm that moves data between chips at 400 gigabits per second, and the article says it is aiming that at TPU v10 orders.
Intel is confirmed for the packaging.

@@FLOW@@Google|decides what to build and places the order|Design partners|Broadcom and MediaTek draw the chip, with chatter that AMD is joining|TSMC|fabricates it on 2nm whoever drew it|Intel|handles the packaging that binds the dies into one part@@Design, fabrication and assembly sit at different companies. That is why trouble at one step lets Google swap out that step alone.

## What TPU v10 settles

Adding designers is not only about price for Google.
The moment Broadcom moved volume to other customers, putting everything through one house became the risk itself.

If AMD's involvement is confirmed, the firm steps for the first time into drawing someone else's AI silicon and picks up a revenue line that does not depend on beating Nvidia with its own.
If nothing is confirmed by the end of 2027, the TPU design seat hardens into a Broadcom and MediaTek split, and the premise behind Jukan's question goes with it.
meru-terafab-fel-euv-light-source-vs-asm:
A signal came out of Terafab, the chip plant Musk is building in Texas, that he intends to make the light that draws the circuits himself.
Only one company in the world can make that light today, ASML of the Netherlands.

@@REF@@Musk signals interest in FEL-EUV for Terafab, potentially cutting power versus ASML's current light source (TrendForce, 2026-08-12)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/12/news-musk-signals-interest-in-fel-euv-for-terafab-potentially-cutting-power-vs-asmls-current-light-source/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/11135042/Terafab-SpaceX-on-X-20260811-624x293.jpg

It started with a night rendering of Terafab that began circulating on X on August 6.
A large ring runs under the building in the picture, and people asked whether that was a machine for pushing electrons to near the speed of light.
Musk answered with three letters and one more: "FEL FTW".

FEL stands for free electron laser.
It is a machine that accelerates electrons very hard and then pulls light out of them.
FTW is internet shorthand for "this is the way", so putting the two together says the light source is going to be an FEL.

## How is EUV light made

Chip circuits are drawn with light.
Drawing them finer takes light of a shorter wavelength, and what the industry uses now is extreme ultraviolet at 13.5 nanometres, EUV.

@@FLOW@@Tin droplets|fired fifty thousand times a second|High-power laser|hits each droplet and burns it into plasma|Curved mirrors|collect the light and send it to the wafer@@It burns metal to get light, which is why it drinks electricity. What Musk wants to replace is the first two steps.

An FEL has no metal to burn.
Light comes out as long as there is force pushing the electrons, and the force given back by decelerating electrons can be returned to push the next ones.
Meru writes that this is why Musk describes the route in terms of free energy.

## Changing the source changes the power bill

@@BAR@@Today's route (tin plasma)|4.4 megawatts|4.4|Free electron laser (theoretical)|0.7 megawatts|0.7@@This is the input power it takes to get one kilowatt of EUV light out. ## Ten metres and one kilometre

Size is the price.
An ASML EUV tool is a little over ten metres long, while a machine that accelerates electrons to pull light out of them runs past a kilometre when it is built for research.
Korea has one, the fourth-generation light source accelerator run by the Pohang Accelerator Laboratory, and Meru notes that it too is more than a kilometre end to end.

Meru's reading is that the arithmetic still has a chance.
One FEL can feed light to dozens of lithography tools, and a machine built to make lithography light rather than research light can be far shorter.

## The number 2028

Musk did not raise the idea of making EUV light with an FEL first.
A US startup chaired by former Intel chief executive Pat Gelsinger is developing the same route, with the US government among its stakeholders.
What that company has promised, though, is also one prototype in 2028.
There is no FEL supplier anywhere that can feed light to volume production.

So the thing being decided now is not whether an FEL can make the light.
It already can.
What is being decided is whether that light is even and steady enough to draw circuits on a wafer, and when that gets confirmed.
If one FEL source clears production lithography inside 2028, ASML's monopoly gets a deadline attached to it for the first time; if the route is still a prototype by then, Terafab joins the queue at ASML like everyone else.

## Why the border and not a fine

Section 337 sits in the Tariff Act of 1930.

@@FLOW@@Complaint|Maxell filed on six patents in December 2024 and lodged an amended complaint on July 24, 2026|Institution|The commission opened docket 337-TA-1516 on August 12, and a target completion date is set within 45 days|Final determination|Unlike a court case that runs through three levels of appeal, this usually concludes in 16 to 18 months|Exclusion order|Customs stops the goods at the border, and inventory already inside the country is frozen by a cease and desist order@@A court collects money from the losing side. @@TIME@@2015-11|Signs a joint development and licensing agreement with Samsung|2023|An East Texas jury awards $303 million for infringement of five patents, with $118 million added in 2024|2026-07|Google, Nvidia, Broadcom and Supermicro are pulled in as co-respondents at the commission|2026-08-05|Samsung settles with a five-year licence worth up to $897 million|>2026-09-26|Deadline for the target completion date in the Maxell case to be set, 45 days after institution@@A settlement Samsung had resisted for three years after the verdict arrived one month after its customers appeared on the respondent list.

On the verdict alone Samsung had no reason to hurry.

bilello-gross-vs-net-interest-1_37t-soci:
Interest charged on US government debt over the past twelve months came to $1.37 trillion, a record.
But lining that number up against Social Security spending to see which is bigger does not work. The two are not measured with the same ruler.

@@REF@@US July deficit tops $432 billion as outlays grow (Reuters, 2026-08-12)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-july-deficit-tops-432-180448445.html|https://storage.googleapis.com/media.mwcradio.com/mimesis/2026-08/12/2026-08-12T180448Z_2_LYNXMPEM7B1FE_RTROPTP_3_USA-TRUMP-LABOR-SENATE.JPG

Reuters reports from the July Monthly Treasury Statement that the month's deficit was $432 billion, a July record, and that the fiscal 2026 shortfall over ten months is $1.799 trillion. Interest is the fastest-growing item inside that gap.

## Interest goes by two names

The "interest expense on the public debt" that Treasury publishes each month adds up the interest on every Treasury security outstanding.
That includes the interest on securities held by the Social Security and Medicare trust funds.

That portion is money the government moves from one pocket to another and writes down as interest.
No cash leaves the government, so the budget does not count it as interest at all.

What the budget carries instead is a different number, net interest, with that portion taken out.
Fiscal 2024 shows the gap plainly. Gross interest was $1.133 trillion and net interest was $880 billion.
In a single year, two figures both called interest sat $253 billion apart.

@@BAR@@Social Security outlays|$1.569T|1569|Gross interest|$1.229T|1229|Net interest in the budget|$1.028T|1028@@The figure Bilello cites is the trailing-twelve-month version of the middle bar. The one that competes with Social Security for size is the bottom bar.@@Fiscal 2025 actuals, CBO Monthly Budget Review (November 2025) and US Treasury Fiscal Data (accessed 2026-08-13)

## Net interest is already number two

Correcting the number does not shrink the story.
In fiscal 2025 Social Security was the largest line at $1.569 trillion, and net interest came next at $1.028 trillion.
Medicare at $992 billion and national defense at $868 billion sat below it.
Interest has already passed health care and defense to become the second-largest item in the budget.

The cause is not only a bigger pile of debt. The price of carrying it went up.
The average rate on marketable Treasury debt rose from 1.5% in July 2021 to 3.4% in July 2026, more than doubling.
Put simply, rolling the same stack of debt costs twice what it cost five years ago, and the stack grew as well.

## CBO does not see it by 2055 either

Everything turns on which ruler you pick up.
Measured gross, the gap to Social Security has already narrowed to under $200 billion and a crossover looks close.
Measured as the budget line, the Congressional Budget Office's long-term outlook puts net interest at 5.4% of gross domestic product in 2055 against 6.0% for Social Security. Three decades out, Social Security is still larger.
Mix the two figures and you get "soon to be first." Use one of them consistently and you get "still second in thirty years."
The books on this fiscal year close in mid-October.
meru-jackson-hole-2026-payments-theme-wa:
The Kansas City Fed has set the theme for this year's Jackson Hole symposium, held August 27 to 29. It is not interest rates. It is "Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy."

@@REF@@Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, accessed 2026-08-13)|https://www.kansascityfed.org/research/jackson-hole-economic-symposium/|https://www.kansascityfed.org/images/GettyImages-1743180766.original.jpg

## The theme is the year's worry

Jackson Hole is a three-day gathering that the Kansas City Fed, one of the twelve regional Federal Reserve banks, has hosted since 1978.
Only about a hundred people are invited, mostly central bank governors and academic economists, and press access is kept deliberately small.
The Kansas City Fed also picks the theme, which is why the theme tends to show what the Fed is worrying about that year.

In 2024 it was "Reassessing the Effectiveness and Transmission of Monetary Policy." In 2025 it was "Labor Markets in Transition: Demographics, Productivity, and Macroeconomic Policy."
How far to move rates, and how work itself is changing, were the questions of the past two years.

This year it is payments.

One step of explanation makes clear why that belongs on a central bankers' agenda.
A stablecoin is a token that moves on a blockchain while its value is pinned one to one to a currency such as the dollar.
That is the definition, and the part central banks care about comes right after it.
Once people start paying each other with the token instead of through a bank account, the question of who controls the payment rails changes hands.
The channel a central bank uses to steer the economy also runs through bank deposits and bank lending, so money that circulates outside that channel is money policy reaches less easily.

## Warsh called it a blank page

Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed chair on May 22, 2026. This is his first Jackson Hole in the job.
